findings.source_en: The disciples snatched him in the night.
findings.issue: المُريد is frozen for Acolyte (Tiel's title) and the glossary note now reserves it explicitly: generic disciples/followers must never use مريد. Disciple is its own frozen term as of the 193-term glossary — الحواريّ, pl. الحواريّون — distinct from Acolyte المُريد, Vassal التابِع and Cultist عابد الطائفة. (Already applied in translated/; kept here so re-application is a no-op.)

The speaker is a frightened child in the prologue (namespace ScaredChild), and the sibling line is plain ('What if Mether doesn't like me?' → ماذا لو لم تُحبّني الأُمَّهة؟). يعتريني الخوف is literary diction — 'fear comes over me' — which no child says. The English is the simplest possible phrasing.

findings.source_en: You’re more than a weapon, Child.
findings.ar: أنت أكثر من سلاح، أيها الطفل.
findings.issue: The same vocative 'Child' addressed to the same character is rendered يا ولدي throughout the Undermether's lines (Dialogue_Dlg_UnderMether_Tower_Interact/B9C83DE3..., 651D7749..., 0D4AB72D...). أيها الطفل is a flat 'O child' and reads colder and more distant than either the English or the corpus's established form; it also sits oddly on a vessel the speaker has just called a weapon.
findings.suggested_ar: أنت أكثر من سلاح، يا ولدي.

findings.source_en: He was once like any mortal.
findings.issue: 'Mortal' is rendered فانٍ elsewhere (Dialogue_Dlg_Hub_Ruk_TowerTop_ExtraHint/CB0C7F6D40F3B6653409DEA65CBD330A, 'But you're no mortal.' → لكنك لستَ فانيًا). The mortality contrast is what this passage turns on — a sibling row in the same namespace is 'Now he's pure.' — and بشر ('human') drops it. أي + the collective بشر is also poor agreement.
